title: A Peasant Woman Digging in Front of Her Cottage

image.credit: Photograph via Wikimedia Commons (Vincent van Gogh - A Peasant Woman Digging in Front of Her Cottage - 1968.92 - Art Institute of Chicago.jpg)

work.text: In Nuenen, the artist also returned to the more monochromatic palette of browns, greens, and grays that he had used in his early years in the Netherlands. He painted a series of cottages— including this painting—based on his walks through the village.

source.author: Art Institute of Chicago
source.title: Collection description: A Peasant Woman Digging in Front of Her Cottage

moment.text: Van Gogh was an admirer of the Realism of Jules Breton, Gustave Courbet and Millet, and he compared his copies to a musician's interpreting Beethoven.

matters.text: I've tried to bring out the idea that these people eating potatoes by the light of their lamp have dug the earth with the self-same hands they are now putting into the dish, and it thus suggests manual labour and - a meal honestly earned.

source.author: Vincent van Gogh
source.title: Letter 404 to Theo van Gogh, Nuenen, c. 30 April 1885
source.publisher: The Complete Letters of Vincent van Gogh, via WebExhibits

matters.lead: On The Potato Eaters, painted the same spring:

matters.text: Van Gogh carefully infused the woman, the cottage, and the setting with the same earthy tones and the loose, directional texture of the brushstrokes. In doing so, he emphasized the way she belonged to this place, and it to her.
